name: The Glowing Fruit
summary: A strange fruit shines among Teldrassil's trees, and its growth troubles those who find it. You carry it to Denalan at Lake Al'Ameth, where the herbalist can study the unfamiliar plant.

sections.title: An Unnatural Harvest
sections.body: In Teldrassil's misty boughs, you may find plants bearing large, round fruit that shine with their own light. The World Tree's balance is delicate, and its wildlife has behaved strangely of late. So unusual plants call for care. You gather the glowing fruit to bring it to someone who knows the wild flora.

sections.title: Denalan's Investigation
sections.body: At Lake Al'Ameth, Denalan receives the glowing fruit with fascination and concern. The gardener and herbalist thinks its seeds may have come from distant lands across the sea, perhaps even the Eastern Kingdoms. Yet he worries more about how the foreign seed has reacted with Teldrassil's soil. When Denalan plants the seeds in prepared earth, hostile boglings rise from it.

faq.q: Where is the Strange Fruited Plant found?
aliases: where do i find the plant
how to start the glowing fruit
faq.answer: The Strange Fruited Plant grows wild in Teldrassil's forest, among the undergrowth and away from the major settlements. Gathering it yields the Glowing Fruit.
Denalan is a night elf herbalist and botanist who lives along the shores of Lake Al'Ameth. He tends the soil, studies local plants, and watches the strange disturbances affecting Teldrassil.

aliases: what is wrong with the fruit
faq.answer: No one knows why the fruit glows. Denalan considers it unusual and plans to study it.

faq.q: What happens when you hand the fruit to Denalan?
faq.answer: You bring the glowing fruit to Denalan at Lake Al'Ameth for examination. His findings and the result of your delivery become clear when you return.

faq.q: Where does Denalan think this plant came from?
faq.answer: Denalan suspects the plant's seeds came from far across the Great Sea, carried to Kalimdor from the distant eastern continent of Azeroth.

faq.q: Does this quest connect to other ecological problems on Teldrassil?
faq.answer: Yes. The plant is part of Denalan's wider study of why Teldrassil's boughs and woodland creatures such as the timberlings have grown more agitated and unnatural.

angles.text: As a druid who guards nature's balance, you know foreign, volatile plants growing in Teldrassil's sacred boughs are cause for concern.
As an herbalist, you can see how foreign seeds may cross continents and change in enchanted soil.
As a night elf, you learn from Denalan that the young soil of your new home, Teldrassil, can suffer unpredictable foreign blights.
